implementation_notes: Codable (a typealias for Encodable & Decodable in the standard library) makes the envelope a four-line generic struct: struct Envelope<Payload: Codable> { let headers: [String: String]; let payload: Payload }, with JSONEncoder/JSONDecoder synthesizing the wire form and CodingKeys customizing field names only when a legacy peer demands it. Application code decodes the envelope and uses env.payload, so the classic wrapper plus manual serialization disappears. On URLSession-style transports the metadata can also ride in URLRequest headers, leaving the body untouched.
pitfalls: Synthesized Codable fails at runtime (DecodingError) for non-conforming field types - a Date without a decoder strategy, for instance - and a generic payload makes the error message indirect.
Envelope<Payload: Codable> cannot decode heterogeneous payloads: a polymorphic envelope needs an enum payload with a manual init(from:), which is where the simple struct stops being simple.
Dictionary-typed headers depend on key ordering only for hashing; a canonical header order must be imposed explicitly if the envelope is signed.
